ui.about.body_art:
Grids, heroes and logos are fetched from SteamGridDB. Without a key the plugin still works, the tiles just stay grey.

How to set it up:
1. Sign in at steamgriddb.com and go to your profile → Preferences → API.
2. Generate a key (it is free) and copy it.
3. Paste it into the plugin's Settings in the Quick Access panel.

For a game that is already added, fetch artwork with the button on its page in this list — that also works if you added the key later.
ui.about.body_cloud:
The cloud is a BACKUP, not the transport. The plugin only reaches for it when the card has nothing to inherit from: a first run of a game on a new device, or a freshly formatted card. Everything else works without a cloud.

How to set it up:
1. Install Ludusavi as a Flatpak: com.github.mtkennerly.ludusavi
2. Open it in Desktop Mode and, in its cloud settings, connect rclone to your provider (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, WebDAV…).
3. Go back to Game Mode. The plugin's Settings will say “cloud configured”.

The plugin does not guess: when there is no configuration it says so rather than pretending everything is in sync.

Cloud sync takes longer than you might expect — roughly 90% of that time is waiting for the provider to answer, not work on this side. That is why the button reports the current stage instead of just “Working…”.

Do not run the decky-ludusavi plugin at the same time: both would push saves to the same cloud and manufacture conflicts.
ui.about.body_info:
The game page of a non-Steam shortcut is empty by nature, because Valve has no data about it. The plugin adds:

• release date, description, genres, publisher and Metacritic score from the Steam store,
• completion times from HowLongToBeat — main story, main plus extras, completionist,
• compatibility with Steam Deck, SteamOS and Steam Machine,
• how many people are playing that game right now.

All of it is fetched ON DEMAND, by a button, never in the background.

When the description belongs to a different edition of the game, point at the right entry with “Pick store game”. This happens because the Ludusavi database ties a title to a single appid: “Grand Theft Auto V” leads to the Legacy edition rather than Enhanced.

The same information appears on Steam's own game page, on a card next to the PLAY button, together with syncing that one game and a jump to its store page. The card can be turned off in Settings — separately for card games and for Steam games.
ui.about.body_playtime:
Steam has no way to store the playtime of a non-Steam shortcut, so the plugin counts it itself and carries the total on the card. The number on the tile is the sum across all devices, not just this one.

• Suspending the device does not count towards playtime.
• When adopting a shortcut you added yourself, the plugin also takes over its Steam playtime — the only trace of sessions from before the plugin.
• Without the card in the reader you only see what the plugin remembered. Playtime numbers never go down, so the total does not jump backwards.
• The per-device breakdown is in the game's details in this list.
ui.about.body_saves:
The transport is the CARD, not the cloud. Without the card you cannot play the game at all, so the card always holds the newest state — and it needs no network. The copy lives in .sdsync/saves on the card itself, so every card carries the saves of its own games.

• When you exit a game the save goes to the card, and then (if you have a cloud) to the cloud. Never the other way round: the cloud never receives a state the card does not have. Otherwise the second device would see “card unchanged”, start from an older save, and have no way to learn about the newer one.
• Restores are considered when the card goes in, after the device starts, when the network comes back, and on demand.
• The saves of a running game are untouchable — checked twice, including immediately before restoring.
• A safety backup is taken outside the cloud loop before every restore.
• When state has drifted, the plugin does NOT overwrite. It shows three timestamps — the save in the game, the copy on the card, the copy in the cloud — and waits for your decision.
• “I don't know” counts as drift, not as “no changes”. An unreadable tool response or a missing network will never be shown as “all good”.
ui.about.body_start:
Games on the card have to sit in a Games/<game name>/… layout — that is where the plugin looks.

1. Insert the card and press “Scan SD card” in the Quick Access panel.
2. Games whose title was not recognised show up in this list under “Unrecognized games”. That is where you type the title by hand or point at the right .exe.
3. Done — the games are in your Steam library with Proton, and their saves travel with the card.

Right after a game is added the plugin checks whether there is a save to restore. That is the one moment when asking is free: the Proton prefix is fresh, so there is nothing to lose, and the card is in the reader.

Cloud, artwork and store metadata are optional — see the categories below.
ui.about.body_tiles:
• The scan walks the folders on the card and picks the game executable itself, skipping installers, redists and crash handlers. If it picks the wrong one, point at the right file with “Pick .exe”.
• The title comes from the Ludusavi database, because save detection hangs off it. The database knows “Baba Is You”, not “Baba is You” — so a hand-typed title goes through it too, and if it is not there the plugin says so instead of going quiet. You can search by a fragment of the name.
• A shortcut you added YOURSELF earlier is ADOPTED, not duplicated. A new shortcut means a new Proton prefix, which means orphaned progress — matching goes by the resolved .exe path, and the adopted shortcut keeps its prefix and its playtime. When several shortcuts match, the plugin does not guess; it asks you.
• A new shortcut gets Proton and artwork, and every card gets a Steam collection named after it.
• The dot on the tile says whether the card is in the reader: green means yes, white means no, and the cover turns greyscale. You choose the corner in Settings, or turn it off.
• Shortcut paths are refreshed on every scan. A card's mount point changes when you rename it and differs between devices, while a Steam shortcut stores the path verbatim — without the refresh the game stops launching.
• A game removed from the card does not vanish quietly: the plugin offers “stop managing” for it, and the save and playtime stay on the card.
ui.about.body_trouble:
Start with “Show event log” in the Quick Access panel. Every operation records what it did and how long it took — it is the only place where the cause of a failure is visible.

• “No info for these games” — Ludusavi does not know that title, so the game has no save support at all. Fix the title with “Change title”; the search works on a fragment of the name.
• A game stops launching after you rename the card — run a scan, it refreshes shortcut paths.
• Drift reported for every game at once — usually no network, or no cloud configured. The log will say which stage failed.
• The dot does not change colour after you remove the card — the plugin polls for this every 10 seconds, give it a moment.
• Changing a game's title requires the card in the reader, and the plugin refuses without it. The title is the game's identity: the name of its backup directory on the card moves with it, so without the card the game would lose its saves.

The plugin only ever moves games from its own registry. Games you bought on Steam, your own shortcuts, emulators and launchers are untouchable.
ui.about.tagline: Non-Steam games on a removable SD card get real library entries, artwork and store metadata — and their saves travel with the card between SteamOS devices.
